title: Cut Lock, Drifting Residual
subtitle: Tampering at Orchard Standpipe and a Precautionary Advisory

brief.userPrompt: Overnight on Saturday the fence-gate contact ZS-612 at Orchard Standpipe tripped and cleared twice and CAM-13 caught a figure near the ladder cage; the roof hatch switch ZS-611 has been out of service since 2024, so RTU-02 still reports the hatch closed, and the site is not due for a visit until Tuesday. The exercise opens on Sunday morning, when the day operator reviews the overnight alarm log and sees the outlet chlorine residual AIT-611 drifting down; the crew sent to the site finds the hatch padlock cut. Sampling under ERP-3, isolating the standpipe from Zone 2, Millbrook police and the FBI, Ohio EPA DDAGW consultation and the precautionary boil-water advisory for the Hilltop area.
constraints: Every email address of the City and the department uses the exercise domain millbrook-oh.example; outside parties use fictional domains and the fictional outlets of the communications plan (Channel 4, the Millbrook Courier); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.
Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (police, the FBI, Ohio EPA DDAGW, the Carver County Health Commissioner, the media) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Physical intrusion at a storage facility, sampling before conclusions, isolation without losing pressure, and a precautionary advisory decided within two hours
overview.threat: Overnight on Saturday someone cut through the fence at Orchard Standpipe (870 Orchard Road), cut the ladder-cage and roof-hatch padlocks and opened the roof hatch. The site’s intrusion detection is thin: the hatch switch ZS-611 has been out of service since a lightning strike in 07/2024 (WO-24-1187), so RTU-02 still reports the hatch closed; the gate contact ZS-612 tripped and cleared twice and was acknowledged as a nuisance alarm; CAM-13 covers the gate only. The outlet chlorine residual AIT-611 has drifted down since about 02:00, and an empty plastic jug lies at the foot of the ladder. Nothing has been confirmed in the water.
overview.operationalImpact: Orchard Standpipe and the Orchard Wellfield feed part of Zone 2 (Hilltop). The department must sample under ERP-3 before anything is drained, isolate the standpipe without dropping Zone 2 below 20 psi (possible while Hilltop Tank stays above 15 ft, with the wells stopped), preserve evidence for Millbrook Police and the FBI, consult Ohio EPA DDAGW and Carver County Public Health, and decide within two hours of the sign of entry on a precautionary advisory — boil water or do not drink, for which streets — without waiting for lab results that take 18 hours (coliform) to three days (chemical screen). A Zone 2 advisory reaches about 42,000 people on a Sunday and needs the City Manager’s approval; lifting it needs two rounds of satisfactory samples 24 hours apart.

overview.targetAudience: Water Operations, Distribution, Water Quality / Lab, Public Information, Security
overview.location: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer, Millbrook, Carver County, Ohio

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Keep Operations, Distribution, the lab, Security and the PIO on one set of facts from the first look at the overnight alarm log to the advisory release, and reach the Annex B critical customers before the public.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Decide within two hours of the sign of entry whether to issue a precautionary advisory, of which type (Boil Water or Do Not Drink) and for which streets, after consulting DDAGW and Public Health, and record the basis on ERP-2 (ERP Sections 8.2 and 9).

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Treat the AIT-611 drift and the site evidence as a possible contamination event: sample per ERP-3 before draining anything, isolate the standpipe without dropping Zone 2 below 20 psi, and preserve video and RTU logs for law enforcement.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Follow ERP Section 8.2, the ERP-3 sampling plan, the PCP 10.3 precautionary template and the Section 9.5 notification sequence, and keep the department, not an outside agency, as the decision-maker for operations and advisories.

roles.name: Director of Water Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages the water system, including treatment plants, pump stations, tanks, and the distribution network, and is responsible for declaring incident levels and issuing advisories in coordination with the Water Quality Manager.
standingOrders: Any sign of entry at a storage site is a Level 2 condition (ERP 8.2).
Decide on a precautionary advisory within two hours of the sign of entry; the decision does not wait for lab results.
Record every advisory decision and its basis on ERP-2 before release; the City Manager approves an advisory over 5,000 people.
Outside agencies advise and investigate; the Director decides on operations and advisories.

roles.name: Distribution Superintendent (Distribution)
roles.description: Owns the distribution system, the storage sites and their valves, field crews, flushing and hydrant sampling access, and pressure in each zone.
standingOrders: Isolate a storage site by its inlet and outlet valves only if no zone drops below 20 psi (ERP 8.2).
Stop the Orchard wells before isolating Orchard Standpipe, or they will fill it to overflow.
Nothing is drained or flushed at a suspected tampering site until it has been sampled (ERP 8.2 step 4).
No crew enters a site where tampering is suspected until Millbrook Police have cleared it.

roles.name: Public Information Officer (PIO)
roles.description: Owns customer notices, boil-water advisories, social media, and the press; responsible for releasing all public statements and managing the Joint Information Center.
standingOrders: No public release before the Annex B critical customers have been called (ERP 9.5).
Use the PCP 10.3 precautionary template; describe the area by streets, not by zone number.
Never say “no contamination” as a conclusion; say what is being tested and when results are due.
Answer posts with the approved lines and the Customer Service number (PCP Section 8).

roles.name: Water Quality Manager (Compliance)
roles.description: Owns sampling, the lab, regulatory reporting, and public-notice triggers; confirms health-effects content and sampling plan behind every advisory.
standingOrders: Sample the facility outlet and the first two hydrants downstream before anything is drained (ERP-3).
Know the turnarounds: field tests 15 minutes, coliform 18–24 hours, chemical screen 48–72 hours.
Consult DDAGW and Carver County Public Health on any precautionary advisory.
Recommend lifting only after two satisfactory rounds 24 hours apart (ERP 8.3, 9.6).

roles.name: Security & Emergency Manager (Security)
roles.description: Owns site security, the law-enforcement liaison, and the emergency response plan; responsible for physical order and evidence preservation.
standingOrders: Call Millbrook Police for any sign of entry; photograph before anyone touches anything.
Preserve MBW-NVR-01 footage (30-day overwrite) and RTU-02 event logs.
Keep a scene log of who enters the site and when.
Report a credible contamination threat to the FBI immediately (ERP Section 5).

phases.title: The Overnight Log
phases.goal: Notice what the overnight alarms and the residual trend mean before anyone has seen the site, and get the right people moving.
beats: At 07:15 the day operator finds two ZS-612 gate trips acknowledged as nuisance alarms overnight and a CAM-13 clip of a figure near the ladder cage.
At 07:25 the AIT-611 trend shows the outlet residual falling since about 02:00 while the wellfield chlorine trim runs flat out.
At 07:35 MBW-NVR-01 reports a CAM-13 recording gap from 02:33 to 03:11.
At 07:45 the SecureLine patrol report says the gate was closed and chained at 05:40; at 07:50 a neighbor posts about a flashlight on the standpipe at 2 a.m.

phases.title: Cut Lock
phases.goal: Confirm the entry, sample before conclusions, and work out how to isolate the standpipe without losing Zone 2 pressure.
beats: At 08:05 the Distribution crew finds the fence cut, the ladder-cage and hatch padlocks cut and an empty jug at the foot of the ladder.
At 08:15 field samples show a low residual at the outlet and a small conductivity rise; at 08:20 Millbrook Police close the site as a crime scene.
At 08:25 a draft notice from the Deputy PIO says “do not drink” for the whole city; at 08:30 Channel 4 asks whether someone poisoned the water.
At 08:35 the Control Room sets out the hydraulics of isolation; at 08:40 the City Manager asks whether 42,000 people really need an advisory.

phases.title: Isolate and Advise
phases.goal: Make the precautionary advisory decision inside the two-hour window, with the lab results still a day or more away.
beats: At 09:00 detectives are on scene; the two-hour mark since the cut lock was found is 10:05.
At 09:05 the Health Commissioner asks the question that decides it: boil water or do not drink? This is the decision point.
At 09:10 the crew explains what closing the standpipe takes; at 09:15 detectives find residue on the hatch frame and call the FBI.
At 09:20 the sampling team learns the contract lab courier does not run until Monday; at 09:25 the critical-customer list for the area comes in.

phases.title: Holding the Line
phases.goal: Run the advisory and the investigation side by side, keep pressure in Zone 2, and answer the public with facts.
beats: At 10:05 the FBI coordinator reports what the field screen did and did not find, and says the advisory is the City’s call.
At 10:15 DDAGW confirms the Tier 1 consultation and the lifting criteria; at 10:20 the RTU-02 event log is exported for the police.
At 10:35 Distribution reports Hilltop Tank falling with the wells off; at 10:40 Channel 4 asks how long this will last.
At 10:58 SecureLine asks about Monday’s patrol schedule.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 07:00 on Sunday, October 25. The day operator has just relieved the night operator in the RWTP Control Room. Demand is low at about 6 MGD; Hilltop Tank reads 27 ft and Orchard Standpipe 84 ft. The weather is clear and cool, 52°F. Distribution has one crew on call and the SecureLine patrol is on its weekend route. No alarms are active.
msel.expectedAction: Each team states its Sunday-morning staffing and how it would be reached.

msel.event: Field Report: Reviewing the overnight alarm summary, the day operator finds that the Orchard Standpipe gate contact ZS-612 tripped and cleared at 01:52 and 02:31; both were acknowledged by the night shift as wind. RTU-02 shows the roof hatch closed, but ZS-611 has been out of service since 07/2024. A CAM-13 clip at 02:29 shows a figure with a flashlight at the edge of the frame, walking from the gate toward the ladder cage.
msel.expectedAction: The IC treats the trips and the clip as a possible sign of entry, has the Distribution on-call crew and Millbrook Police sent to the site (ERP 8.2), and asks the Water Quality Manager to look at AIT-611; Security has the CAM-13 footage preserved before the 30-day overwrite.

msel.event: Phone Call: Health Commissioner Dr. Anita Shah: “I’ll support a precautionary advisory, but you have to pick the type. If someone put a chemical in that standpipe, boiling doesn’t help and can make some things worse — that’s a Do Not Drink. If it’s a contamination threat you can’t characterize, Do Not Drink is the cautious answer, but it means bottled water for thousands of people tonight. What are you issuing, and for which streets?”

metrics.name: Recognition and Site Response
metrics.fail: The overnight trips were dismissed as wind because the night shift did; no crew or police were sent before the 08:00 jump; evidence (CAM-13, RTU-02) was not preserved.
metrics.pass: The crew and Millbrook Police were sent after I-01, CAM-13 footage was exported after I-03 and Level 2 was declared at the sign of entry (I-05).
metrics.excellence: The team linked the AIT-611 trend (I-02) to the gate trips before the crew arrived, recorded 08:05 as the start of the two-hour clock, and kept a scene log from the first entry.

metrics.name: Sampling and Isolation
metrics.fail: Something was drained or flushed before it was sampled, or the standpipe was closed with the wells running; Zone 2 pressure or Hilltop Tank was not watched.
metrics.pass: ERP-3 sampling came before any flushing (I-06), the wells were stopped and the standpipe isolated under police escort (I-08, I-09b), and a booster trigger level was set (I-16).
metrics.excellence: The team negotiated the escorted entry at I-06b without losing the evidence, planned for the Sunday courier gap (I-10b) and told the PIO the realistic lifting time.

metrics.name: Advisory Decision
metrics.fail: No advisory decision was made by 10:05, or one was made without DDAGW and Public Health, without an area drawn by streets, or without the City Manager’s approval and an ERP-2 record.
metrics.pass: The Director and the Water Quality Manager decided the type and area at I-10, consulted DDAGW and Public Health, had the City Manager approve and recorded the basis on ERP-2 before 10:05.
metrics.excellence: The choice between Boil Water and Do Not Drink was argued from the evidence (residual drop, conductivity, residue), critical customers were called before release, and the FBI field screen (I-14b) was not treated as a clearance.

metrics.name: Public Information
metrics.fail: The Deputy PIO’s draft (I-07) or anything like it was released; the PIO confirmed a substance or promised a lifting time that could not be met.
metrics.pass: The PIO held I-07, answered I-07b and I-16b from facts, used the PCP 10.3 template with street boundaries and answered the I-13 rumor without repeating it.
metrics.excellence: The PIO coordinated with Millbrook Police on what not to say, gave a next-update time every time and set expectations from the DDAGW lifting criteria (I-15).

hotwash.methodDescription: Each team names three things that went well and three that did not; the facilitator writes them up and looks for the same issue in more than one team.

questions.text: Two gate trips were acknowledged as wind and the patrol saw “nothing unusual.” What would have caught this at 02:00 instead of 07:15?
ERP 8.2 says the advisory decision does not wait for lab results. When did your clock start, when did you decide, and what was the deciding fact?
Which advisory did you choose and for which streets? What would have changed your mind?
How did you reconcile the police scene with the need to close the standpipe valves? Who made that call?
What did you tell Summit Care, Channel 4 and the public about how long this would last, and was it realistic given the lab timeline?

simcellScripts.trigger: A player asks for access to the site, or for the police view of the threat.
hardQuestions: Who has been inside that fence since 07:00, and is it written down?
Your crew wants to close a valve inside my scene. Why can’t it wait an hour?
Did anyone touch the jug or the hatch?
concessions: Escorts one crew member to the valve vault once told isolation protects the public and stays off the roof.
Shares what the department needs for its advisory, but never confirms a substance to the press.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Ohio EPA DDAGW district engineer (Paul Grieve)
simcellScripts.trigger: The Water Quality Manager consults DDAGW, or no one has by 09:30.
hardQuestions: What is the area, by streets? How many people?
Boil Water or Do Not Drink — and why that one for an uncharacterized threat?
What is your sampling plan, and when will you have two satisfactory rounds?
concessions: Concurs with a precautionary advisory and records the Tier 1 consultation.
Advises; the advisory decision stays with the Director.

simcellScripts.trigger: Customer Service or the PIO calls with the advisory.
hardQuestions: Lunch is at 11:30 for 120 residents. What do I cook with?
Can my residents shower? Some are on oxygen and can’t go without bathing.
concessions: Follows the advisory once told what to do and when the next call will come.

criticalResources: Orchard Standpipe (LIT-611, AIT-611) and its valve vault
Hilltop Tank level (LIT-601) and Zone 2 pressure
ERP-3 field tests, coliform incubation and the chemical-screen courier
CAM-13 footage on MBW-NVR-01 and the RTU-02 event log
Map of record: streets fed by the standpipe
Annex B critical customers in the area (Summit Care, Millbrook High School, home dialysis)
MillbrookAlert, the City website and the Customer Service line
Bottled-water supply for a Do Not Drink area
